## Historical audit — S0029, visible chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_113438548/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The reference and rendered images are not visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 | Reconstruct a 341 × 512 indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, materials and occlusions. The student's code names an antique workshop display; that semantic interpretation is not independent evidence of the image's contents. |
| Initial build — student response and execute, lines 3–4 | Code constructs multiple objects: a pier and display, wheel and dies, saw, pliers, vise, two chucks, door, window, bench and pipe. Parts are positioned as separate primitives, with hubs, supports and jaws; their actual contact or fit is not geometrically verified. Colors, roughness and attempted bevels are specified, but the initial code has no image textures. It sets a camera and two area lights. No human pose is represented. |
| Failure and repair — execution result line 5; student request line 6; response/execute lines 8–9 | Step 1 failed before producing an image because `scene.world` was `None`. The runner sent that traceback to the student. The revised program creates a world if absent and changes camera position, lens and sensor fit. This is observable adoption of **runner error feedback**, not teacher advice. |
| Validation — execution result line 10, characters [0,88589); select line 11 | Step 2 reports `ok: true`, saves a render and blend file, and is selected. Its actual render log says 16 samples, despite 48 requested in code. Successful execution does not establish visual fidelity. |
| Autonomous revision — student request line 12, characters [0,120348); session line 13; response/execute lines 14–15 | The request supplied both reference and step-2 render for comparison. The student then changed the camera to the opposite side, reduced lighting and palette brightness, raised the bench and window sill, revised tool depth and chuck parts, and added procedural noise and bump materials. These are executed changes; their reasons and visual effectiveness are not directly stated. The session reports zero tool calls. |
| Latest visible result — execution result line 16, characters [0,88212); select line 17 | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, saves a render and blend file, and is selected. The log again reports 16 samples, although the program requests 64. No independent comparison or final formal assessment is visible. |

**Teacher and outcome.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or student receipt of teacher input appears in this visible chunk. This is a student trajectory, not a teacher-only trace. The first execution had a technical failure; subsequent builds succeeded technically. The overall reconstruction outcome and any formal success, partial correctness, or algorithm failure remain **unknown**; this was not an empty patch.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a traceback can support a targeted environment repair, while successful rendering is distinct from matching a reference. Camera-side, lighting, object-height and procedural-texture changes are task-specific experiments, not proven improvements. Whether objects connect correctly, their poses and occlusions match, materials look appropriate, or framing and illumination improved remains unresolved without the unseen images and later chunk.
